Diagnostics and Reporting

Source: vignettes/diagnostics-reporting.Rmd
diagnostics-reporting.Rmd

diagnostics() describes localization and estimator-specific support from a fitted object without refitting nuisance models. The examples below show the returned tables and how to interpret them. Diagnostics do not verify the paper’s inference conditions; distance-tie averaging can change support and concentration, and inference with persistent distance ties is not established.

Nonparametric Regression 

demo_np <- np_demo_data(n = 120, p = 2, design = "sinusoidal", seed = 1)

fit_np <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = demo_np$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "ess")
)

d_np <- diagnostics(fit_np)
as.data.frame(d_np)[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "weighted_mean_y",
  "weighted_sd_y",
  "weighted_y_q50"
)]
#>          target_id    n_eff weighted_mean_y weighted_sd_y weighted_y_q50
#> target_1  target_1 51.84209         0.08698       0.54151      0.1091348

For NP fits, weighted_mean_y equals the local mean estimate when the weights are normalized.

Question Fields to inspect Interpretation
Is weight concentrated? n_eff, max_weight, top-weight shares Concentration, not a count of neighbors; signed TDNN concentration is not probability-weight ESS.
How far does localization reach? Rank radii and weighted distance summaries Depend on the selected metric; CATE/CLATE physical radii use original Euclidean coordinates.
Are both binary arms represented? Arm mass and within-arm ESS CATE uses treatment arms; CLATE uses instrument arms. Read mass and concentration together.
How dispersed is the local outcome? weighted_sd_y and outcome quantiles Outcome spread, not uncertainty about the estimated mean. Negative TDNN weights do not define these probability summaries.
Is ratio inference available? CLATE components, first stage and statuses Inspect these alongside the ratio; see the paired-inference guide.

For NP/TDNN and CATE, nobs() counts training observations. Candidate summaries use minimum ESS and maximum weight/concentration over targets; target rows retain each profile’s values.

CATE Overlap 

demo_cate <- cate_demo_data(n = 150, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 2)

fit_cate <- cate_dnn(
  data = demo_cate$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  t_col = "D",
  m0_col = "m0_oracle", m1_col = "m1_oracle",
  e_col = "e_oracle",
  x0 = demo_cate$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "psi", "nuisance")
)

d_cate <- diagnostics(fit_cate)
as.data.frame(d_cate)[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "treated_mass",
  "control_mass",
  "treated_share",
  "weighted_mean_propensity",
  "treated_ess", "control_ess", "weighted_propensity_q10",
  "weighted_propensity_q90", "top5_score_share"
)]
#>          target_id    n_eff treated_mass control_mass treated_share
#> target_1  target_1 64.96742    0.4291109    0.5708891     0.4291109
#>          weighted_mean_propensity treated_ess control_ess
#> target_1                0.4935985    28.38508    36.59798
#>          weighted_propensity_q10 weighted_propensity_q90 top5_score_share
#> target_1               0.3696287               0.6065485        0.2167448

Overlap diagnostics are available when the fit was constructed from treatment and propensity inputs. If cate_dnn() was called with only a direct pseudo_outcome, overlap fields remain present but are marked unavailable.

treated_ess and control_ess normalize weights within their treatment arm before measuring concentration. An arm with one positive-weight observation has ESS one even if that observation receives tiny total weight; an arm with zero weight has NA ESS. Read these fields alongside treated_mass and control_mass: arm ESS describes concentration within an arm, while arm mass is the total localization weight assigned to that arm.

Printing summarizes available arm information, propensity quantiles and top-five absolute score-contribution shares; the data frame retains each profile’s values. CLATE distinguishes instrument support, clipped propensity mass and squared jackknife-contribution concentration. These quantities have different definitions and should not be interpreted interchangeably. Clipping prevents undefined arithmetic but does not establish overlap. The reported order fraction is descriptive, rather than a calibrated validity threshold.

Experimental PLQR conditioning

PLQR diagnostics and specialized plots remain experimental.

demo_plqr <- plqr_demo_data(n = 160, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 3)

fit_plqr <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo_plqr$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"),
  g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  density_col = "density_oracle",
  theta_eval = demo_plqr$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5,
  x0 = demo_plqr$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = TRUE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "score", "ess")
)

d_plqr <- diagnostics(fit_plqr)
as.data.frame(d_plqr)[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "gram_min_eig",
  "gram_condition_number",
  "jacobian_min_singular_value",
  "jacobian_condition_number",
  "theta_vcov_available"
)]
#>          target_id    n_eff gram_min_eig gram_condition_number
#> target_1  target_1 69.34251     0.286607              1.333248
#>          jacobian_min_singular_value jacobian_condition_number
#> target_1                   0.5965432                  1.274692
#>          theta_vcov_available
#> target_1                 TRUE

The PLQR Gram diagnostic is based on the localized residual-regressor matrix D - m_D(X). It is an identification and conditioning diagnostic, not a local bread estimate.

Tuning Metadata

When a fit uses tuning = ..., the diagnostics table exposes compact tuning metadata without duplicating the full candidate grid into every row.

fit_tuned <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = demo_np$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  tuning = tuning_dnn_paper(lambda = 1.25),
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "tuning")
)

d_tuned <- diagnostics(fit_tuned)
as.data.frame(d_tuned)[, c(
  "target_id",
  "tuning_name",
  "tuning_default_s",
  "tuning_grid_n_candidates",
  "tuning_lambda_default"
)]
#>          target_id       tuning_name tuning_default_s tuning_grid_n_candidates
#> target_1  target_1 paper_undersmooth               45                        5
#>          tuning_lambda_default
#> target_1                  1.25

attr(d_tuned, "tuning_grid")
#>   candidate_id computed_key is_default feasible reason status lambda  s
#> 1         s_45         s_45       TRUE     TRUE     ok     ok     NA 45
#> 2   lambda_0p3         s_10      FALSE     TRUE     ok     ok   0.30 10
#> 3   lambda_0p4         s_14      FALSE     TRUE     ok     ok   0.40 14
#> 4   lambda_0p5         s_18      FALSE     TRUE     ok     ok   0.50 18
#> 5  lambda_0p75         s_27      FALSE     TRUE     ok     ok   0.75 27

Use attr(d_tuned, "tuning_grid") when you need the full candidate table.

Availability Rules

  • Missing W prevents NP/TDNN, CATE and PLQR target diagnostics. Stored grid summaries and paired-ratio/CLATE diagnostics have their own retained state.
  • Rank radii and weighted metric distances require retained dx; otherwise those fields are NA with distance_diagnostics_available = FALSE. CATE/CLATE physical radii can still use retained observations in original units.
  • If CATE treatment/propensity state is unavailable, overlap fields are present but marked unavailable.
  • If PLQR residual-regressor state is unavailable, Gram fields are present but marked unavailable.

The paper states the conditions for inference. These diagnostics do not check all of them.

Using diagnostics in scripts

Warnings summarize one issue family per public call. Independent reports or plots can warn again. Base R warning controls and calling handlers apply, including options(warn = 2). To silence only the tie advisory, use suppressWarnings(fit_call, classes = "rdistnn_distance_ties_warning").

Paired-ratio/CLATE calls retain every target, including unavailable ratios or intervals, and point to status and components. Negative denominators alone are descriptive; deliberately disabled uncertainty does not warn. Ordinary mean fits instead stop on nonfinite computed estimates and request rescaling. Dashboards may omit absent optional extras; invalid options, inconsistent state and unexpected rendering failures stop.

Cause Condition identity
Invalid input rdistnn_input_error
Invalid extension return value rdistnn_callback_error
Computed numerical-range failure rdistnn_numerical_error
Missing optional extra rdistnn_extra_unavailable
Invalid retained state, requiring refitting rdistnn_state_error
Package warning rdistnn_warning, with a family such as rdistnn_distance_ties_warning or rdistnn_partial_result_warning

Owned conditions carry a semantic code and applicable public argument, expected/actual facts and bounded operation name, without storing the full call or its data. Handle recognized identities rather than parsing English messages. Unexpected callback, native and resource errors retain their identities. Unknown character return entries warn and are ignored; missing or noncharacter selectors are input errors.

Read notice facts without displaying warnings

fit$meta$target_notices retains target_id, distance_ties, weight_concentration and weak_localization; meta$n_tied_targets and meta$n_weak_targets retain totals. These fields are available even with return = character() and survive serialization. Candidates describe their selected weights. Concentration is 1 / sum(w^2) from final observation weights; for signed TDNN it is descriptive rather than probability-weight ESS. The weak-localization guide is at least .9 * n with n >= 2, not a validity test. Complete current fitted state is required before reuse.
